info.title: Project Browser control-plane API
info.description: Contracts: /v1 prefix, opaque ids, cursor pagination (max 100), If-Match/expected_version optimistic concurrency, Idempotency-Key on lease acquisition, snapshot commit, local workspace import and automation jobs. Authentication: OIDC sign-in in the system browser (Authorization Code + PKCE), then API session tokens (ADR-0013); or an API token (`Authorization: Bearer pbt_…`, ADR-0017) on the routes marked "API tokens: yes", acting as its owner within its scopes and restrictions. Authorization: organization role combined with client/profile grants, deny by default; identifiers outside the caller’s reach answer 404 exactly like nonexistent ones.

apiToken.description: API token (milestone 10). Only routes marked "API tokens: yes" accept it.

get.description: Identity provider settings for the desktop sign-in (system browser, Authorization Code + PKCE).

post.description: Enroll this device and start a session with a fresh ID token from the identity provider (used once). Returns the session tokens; keep the refresh token in the OS keychain.

get.description: Devices enrolled for the signed-in account (most recent first, at most 100).

post.description: grant_type=refresh_token rotates the refresh token (presenting a previous one ends the session). grant_type=id_token signs in again on an enrolled device (for example to confirm a sensitive action).
Ends the current session (its refresh token stops working). The device stays enrolled; local data is untouched.

Signs a device out everywhere: its sessions end and it cannot refresh or call the API again until it is enrolled anew. Profiles it had open are released from it (a new fencing token). Local browser data on that device is not deleted (the server cannot reach it).

get.description: Organizations the caller belongs to, with the number of profiles they can see in each. Local workspaces exist only on the device and are not listed.

post.description: Creates an organization with the caller as its owner. Requires a verified e-mail address.

get.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply).

patch.description: Change a member’s role (admin, operator, viewer or billing). Only owners may change an owner’s role; ownership itself moves through /ownership-transfer. Requires If-Match or expected_version.

delete.description: Remove a member (or leave, when it is yourself). Their grants are removed with the membership and their access ends at the next request. The last owner cannot be removed.

post.description: Makes another member an owner and the caller an admin. Requires a sign-in within the last few minutes (REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED otherwise) and the target membership version.
Invite an e-mail address with a role. The token in the response is shown only once; send it to the person. Creating a new invitation for the same address withdraws the previous open one.
Withdraws an open invitation (no effect on one already withdrawn or expired).

get.description: What an invitation link leads to, and whether the signed-in account can accept it.

for_this_account.description: Whether the caller's verified e-mail matches the invitation.

post.description: Join the organization. Single use; refused when expired or withdrawn, and when the signed-in account’s verified e-mail is not the invited address.

get.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply).
API tokens: yes (scopes apply).

patch.description: Rename, recolour or archive. Requires If-Match: "<version>" or body.expected_version.

post.description: Grant a member one client (with all its profiles) or one profile.

patch.description: Changes what a grant allows: launch (open, including uploading the session), edit (configuration) and backup_download (restore). Removing launch from someone who has a profile open ends that session.

get.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Profiles the caller can see, oldest first; optional name search and client filter.

post.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply).

get.description: Configuration export (names, client, notes) of up to 10000 profiles. No browser data or session material. Owners and admins only, after a sign-in within 10 minutes.

post.description: Set the client of, or delete, up to 500 profiles. Each id gets its own outcome; ids outside the caller’s reach report not_found, profiles open on a device report in_use (delete only).

get.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply).

patch.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Requires If-Match: "<version>" or body.expected_version. Stale versions return 409.

delete.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Requires If-Match: "<version>". Refused while the profile is open on a device (LEASE_HELD).

post.description: Acquire the profile lease for a device. Requires Idempotency-Key.
Release with the current fencing token. Releasing an already-released lease is a no-op.

get.description: Who has the profile open right now (null: nobody). Uncertain sessions are included.

post.description: Takes the profile for this device (Idempotency-Key required): checks membership, the launch capability, the plan and the browser, then issues a new fencing token. 409 LEASE_HELD while someone has it open; 409 LEASE_UNCERTAIN when the last session ended without closing (ask that person to open the app, or an admin to force a takeover).

Keeps the lease (every 15 s; it lasts 60 s past the last heartbeat) and reports the run state. Returns teammates’ open requests. A holder whose lease expired without anyone else taking it gets it back (revived). 409 FENCING_TOKEN_STALE once it was taken over, revoked or replaced (safe_details.state): stop the browser and keep the local copy aside. 404/403 when access was removed.

Gives the profile back (holder only, current fencing token), optionally with a handoff note for the next person. Allowed after expiry: the holder confirms its browser closed. Releasing twice is a no-op. Open requests for the profile are answered (fulfilled).

Asks the person who has the profile open to hand it over (optional note, no passwords). It never closes their session: they choose when to close and hand off. One open request per person and profile; requests expire after 4 hours.

get.description: Requests for this profile from the last 24 hours, newest first.
The caller’s requests (mine=true) or requests addressed to the caller as holder, from the last 24 hours.

post.description: The person who has the profile open says not now (the requester sees it).
The requester withdraws the request.

Owners and admins end someone’s session or uncertain lease (reason required, confirm: true). A new fencing token fences the old device out: nothing it still sends is written, and its unsynced copy is kept aside on that computer (and as a recovery copy if it uploads one). The other browser may still be open: this cannot stop activity on websites there.

get.description: Uploads kept from devices that lost their session (taken over or revoked), newest first. Owners and admins can restore one as a separate copy; they are erased after the trash period.

One client at a glance: the profiles the caller can see (counts never include hidden ones), who has them open, open tasks, shared bookmarks, and — for owners and admins — who works on it and recent app activity.
Tasks of a client the caller can see, soonest due first (status: open (default), done, all).

post.description: Adds a task. Members with grants add tasks to profiles they can see (or to the whole client with a client grant) and assign them to themselves only. Completing a task never means anything happened on a website.

patch.description: Edits or ticks off a task (If-Match: "<version>").

delete.description: Deletes a task (owners, admins, or whoever created it).

get.description: Shared bookmarks of a client (start-page templates), in their order.

post.description: Adds a shared bookmark (owners and admins): http or https only, at most 50 per client.

patch.description: Renames, re-links or reorders a bookmark (owners and admins; If-Match: "<version>").

get.description: The organization's browser extension policy. Every member's app reads it to judge the extensions installed in organization profiles (off: inventory only; warn; enforce: such profiles open with extensions turned off).

put.description: Replaces the extension policy (owners and admins; If-Match: "<version>").
A device reports the extensions installed in its copy of a profile (names, versions, sources and the permissions they declare; never browsing data). Latest report per profile and device.

get.description: Every extension devices reported in organization profiles: versions, sources, declared permissions (sensitive ones marked), and in how many profiles and devices (owners and admins).
Your API tokens in this organization (all=true: everyone’s, needs tokens.manage). Secrets are never shown again. API tokens cannot call this route.

post.description: Creates a token for yourself. Each scope must be within your role; listed clients and profiles must be within your reach. The answer contains the secret once (`pbt_…`); store it in a secret manager. The token acts as you: if your access shrinks, so does the token’s; if you leave, it stops.
Issues a new secret for your own token (returned once). The previous secret keeps working for grace_minutes (default 60, at most 1440) so integrations can switch without downtime.

delete.description: Revokes a token at once (yours, or anyone’s with tokens.manage). Revoking twice is a no-op. Jobs it queued that have not started fail with ACCESS_REMOVED when a computer would pick them up.

get.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). The calling token: scopes, restrictions, expiry. Useful to check what an integration may do. Interactive sign-ins get 404.
API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Approved sites (where job steps may go) and the running-job limit.

put.description: Owners and admins (automation.manage). Approved sites: `https://app.example.com`, `https://*.example.com`, `http://localhost:3000` (scheme, host, optional port). Jobs whose addresses are not approved are refused; queued jobs are checked again when a computer picks them up. Requires If-Match or expected_version.

post.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Scope: automation:run. Idempotency-Key required: a repeated request answers the same job (200, idempotent-replayed: true); the same key with a different body is refused. The profile must be one you may open (grant capability launch); every address must be on the approved sites. The first step must open an address. keep_open_minutes keeps the profile open after the steps (a launch request) until canceled; debug (automation:debug, owners and admins) hands that session to a local Playwright script.

get.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Scope: automation:read. Jobs on profiles you can see, newest first. state: a state, `active` (queued, claimed, running) or `finished`.
API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Scope: automation:read. The job, its steps (with typed outputs) and its screenshots.

post.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Scope: automation:run. A queued job ends at once. A running job is asked to stop: its computer closes the profile safely (the closing backup still uploads) and reports CANCELED; a profile kept open after its steps closes and the job SUCCEEDED (a stop request). Your own jobs, or any with automation.manage. Canceling twice is a no-op; a finished job answers JOB_FINISHED.

get.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Scope: automation:read. A diagnostic screenshot (image/jpeg or image/png). Kept 7 days. Screenshots can show whatever the page showed: treat them as confidential.

post.description: Lets this computer run jobs (automation.agent), as you: only profiles you may open. accepts: `mine` (only jobs you or your tokens asked for, the default) or `org` (any member’s jobs you may run). Enrolling again updates the name and settings. Debugging sessions are allowed only from the computer itself.

get.description: API tokens: yes (scopes apply). Scope: automation:read. Computers that run jobs: online state, owner, what they accept.

patch.description: Rename, turn off/on, change what it accepts or how many jobs at once. Your own computers, or any with automation.manage. A computer turned off takes no new jobs; running ones finish. Requires If-Match or expected_version.

delete.description: Removes a computer (yours, or any with automation.manage). Jobs it claimed return to the queue; jobs running there end (ACCESS_REMOVED) and that computer closes their profiles safely.

post.description: The computer itself, every 5 s (outbound; nothing listens on it). Heartbeat for its running jobs, new jobs up to its capacity (fair across requesters; never a profile that is open anywhere or already has a running job), cancellations, and jobs it should drop. A claim not started within 60 s returns to the queue.

The computer holding the job reports, in order: `started` (its session lease: id and fencing token; the job becomes RUNNING), `step_started` before each step (refused unless the lease is still current — except closing, which only records how the profile was given back — and the steps before it finished), `step_finished` with typed outputs only, and `finished`. `released` gives a claim back before anything ran (it returns to the queue). Reports from another computer or an older claim answer JOB_CLAIM_STALE. The answer says whether a cancel was requested.

put.description: The computer running a screenshot step uploads the image (image/jpeg or image/png, at most 1.5 MiB) before reporting the step finished with the returned artifact_id. A repeated upload for the same step replaces the previous one.

post.description: Adds an endpoint. The answer contains the signing secret once (`whsec_…`). Deliveries are signed (Standard Webhooks headers webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature), retried with backoff (7 retries over about a day) and then kept as dead letters you can redeliver. The same event id is sent on every retry: deduplicate on it.

patch.description: Change the address, description or events, or turn it off/on (turning on an endpoint that was turned off for failing resets its failure count). Requires If-Match or expected_version.

delete.description: Removes the endpoint and its delivery history; nothing more is sent to it.

post.description: A new signing secret (returned once). For grace_minutes (default 60, at most 1440) every delivery carries two signatures, one per secret, so the receiver can switch without missing events.
Queues a `webhook.test` event for this endpoint only (signed like any other).

get.description: Deliveries to this endpoint, newest first (kept 30 days). state=dead lists the dead letters.

post.description: Sends a delivery again (a dead letter, or one already delivered) with the same event id and body: receivers that deduplicate on webhook-id ignore it if they already processed it.

Starts an encrypted snapshot upload. Requires Idempotency-Key and the live lease. Returns a fresh data key (shown once to this device; a replay of the same request returns the same upload) and upload limits.
Signed URLs (valid 900 s) to upload the named parts of this device's upload. Needs the live lease.

get.description: Parts the storage already holds for this device’s upload (to resume after an interruption).

post.description: Declares the uploaded object (SHA-256, sizes, parts) and hands it to verification (202). Repeating a commit returns the operation as it is. 409 VERSION_CONFLICT when another device committed first.
Cancels this device’s unfinished upload (the profile keeps its last committed snapshot).

get.description: State of one upload (uploading, verifying, committed, failed, canceled, expired).
Committed snapshots of one profile (version history), newest first.

post.description: Authorizes restoring one committed snapshot (default: the newest): a signed download URL and the data key, for this device only. Needs snapshot.restore; every plan is audited.

get.description: Retention, trash period, storage quota and usage of the organization’s snapshots.

patch.description: Changes retention days and the trash period (owners and admins). Quotas are not editable here.

get.description: Deleted profiles that can still be restored, most recently deleted first.

post.description: Restores a deleted profile from the trash (with its snapshots).

get.description: The organization’s key versions (never the keys themselves) and how many snapshots each holds.

post.description: Rotates the organization key (owners; needs a recent sign-in). Existing snapshots are re-wrapped in the background without re-uploading; the old version is destroyed after it is no longer used.
Import a local workspace’s clients and profiles (metadata). dry_run=true returns the plan without changes; dry_run=false requires Idempotency-Key and creates everything atomically.

outcome.description: Organization profiles always get a new server id; the device keeps its local record.
Organization profiles always get a new server id; the device keeps its local record.

get.description: The plan, effective state (trial, active, past_due, grace, restricted, canceled) with its reason and end, limits and features (with staff overrides), current usage and exceeded limits. From the database only.

Plans this server can sell (newest version of each purchasable plan) and the organization’s current plan. Prices are read from the payment provider for display; checkout always shows the binding amount.

amount_minor.description: In the currency’s smallest unit, as configured in the provider.

post.description: Starts the payment provider’s hosted checkout for a plan (owners). Refused while a subscription is live (ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED: change plans in the portal). Open the returned address in a browser; the subscription changes only when the provider confirms payment, never because of the redirect back.

url.description: Hosted page of the payment provider; open it in a browser.

post.description: Opens the payment provider’s customer portal (owners): change plan, payment method, cancel, invoices. Changes made there reach this application through the provider’s webhooks.

url.description: Hosted page of the payment provider; open it in a browser.

get.description: Usage in the current period from the usage ledger (idempotent events: committed backups, finished jobs, API-token requests; daily samples of storage, active profiles and seats) and the last 30 days by day.
Invoices and receipts mirrored from the payment provider (newest first, at most 24).
The provider-hosted invoice page and PDF of one invoice. The desktop opens them in the default browser (after checking the host); the manager window never receives them.
Where checkout and the portal send the browser back. Informational only: a redirect never changes a subscription (the provider’s confirmation does).
The support console’s own OIDC client (Authorization Code + PKCE in the browser).

post.description: Exchanges a fresh ID token of the console client (used once) for a staff token (30 minutes, no refresh). Only active staff; the sign-in must be recent.
Ends this staff session.

get.description: Finds organizations by id, payment provider customer id, or a member’s exact e-mail address (audited).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: An organization id, a provider customer id, or a member’s exact e-mail address.

get.description: Billing overview of one organization: plan, state, dates, limits and usage numbers, provider references, history, invoices, provider events and alerts. No member e-mails, profile names or session data.

post.description: Asks for time-bound access to an organization’s members or activity log, with a reason. A different support lead must approve it.

get.description: Support leads see every request; others see their own. Newest first (at most 100).

post.description: A support lead approves or denies a pending request (never their own). Approval starts the clock; the organization’s activity log records it.
Ends an approved or pending request early (its requester or a support lead).

get.description: Members with e-mail and role — only with approved, unexpired `members` access (recorded).
The organization’s last 100 activity entries (action, outcome, actor id, target type — no details) — only with approved, unexpired `activity` access (recorded).
Entitlement overrides of the organization (newest first).

post.description: Adds an entitlement override (billing admins only): a limit, a feature or unrestricted access, with a reason and an expiry within 90 days. Recorded in the platform audit and the organization’s activity log.
Ends an override now (billing admins only).
Asks the worker to confirm this organization’s subscription with the payment provider now.

get.description: Reconciliation alerts (open first).

post.description: Marks an alert handled (billing admins only).

get.description: The platform audit (staff sign-ins, searches, views, access decisions, overrides): last 200.

post.description: Payment provider webhook (provider-authenticated: `Stripe-Signature` over the exact raw body, 5-minute tolerance). Each event id is recorded once (a duplicate answers 200 and changes nothing); no payload is stored. The worker then fetches the current object from the provider and applies it.
